fromRows.explanation: Builds one LibreOffice Calc workbook from a numeric table typed directly into the document: a Data sheet with your column labels and rows, and a Summary sheet with count, sum, mean, minimum, maximum and sample standard deviation per column. It publishes analysis.xlsx, analysis.ods (reopened by a second Calc process) and data.csv, each checked against independent arithmetic. Choose it for small reproducible tables (2 to 10,000 rows, 1 to 64 columns); use readCSV when the table already exists as a file or comes from another workflow step.
pitfalls: Every cell must be a finite number within ±1e100; text, booleans, blanks and formulas are rejected (INVALID_TABLE).
Column labels are only labels: a label such as "Force (N)" does not convert units or affect any calculation.
Workbook formatting, custom formulas, macros and charts are not produced; only the fixed Data and Summary sheets exist.

readCSV.explanation: Builds the same Data/Summary workbook as fromRows, but reads the table from an existing comma-separated file: the first line holds column labels and every later line holds numbers. The file bytes are copied into the run so later verification does not depend on the original file. Choose it for measured data already on disk or for a numeric table produced by another workflow step (for example an R or ngspice results table).
pitfalls: The path must be absolute; relative paths are rejected during planning.
The CSV must be UTF-8, comma-delimited, at most 8 MiB, with at least two data rows and no empty, text, NaN or infinite cells.
Rows must all have the same number of values as the header; there is no padding or column type guessing.

fromTypedRows.explanation: Builds an editable LibreOffice Calc workbook from a labelled table written in this document: each column is declared as text or number, and each record mixes part or sample IDs, notes and measurements. Missing measurements are explicit nulls that become blank cells, so blank, zero and text stay distinct. It publishes analysis.xlsx, analysis.ods (reopened by a second Calc process) and a typed data.csv handoff, each checked cell by cell, with fixed numeric summaries only for the number columns. Choose it for small reproducible inventories or measurement logs; use fromRows when every cell is a number, and readTypedCSV when the table already exists as a file. Workbook numbers keep 15 significant digits, so Data cells and the Summary MIN and MAX are checked to a relative 1e-14, while SUM, AVERAGE and STDEV allow relative 2e-8 plus 1e-12 of the column's largest magnitude; counts are exact and an all-zero column accepts only zero statistics.
pitfalls: Every cell must match its column: a number column rejects text such as "5" and a text column rejects 123, so quote IDs like "00123".
Empty text is rejected because native reopening would turn it into a blank; use null for a missing value.
Text beginning with =, +, - or @ stays literal text; no formula is ever authored or evaluated.
Units are only part of the column name; nothing is converted, and dates, currency and time zones are not interpreted.

readTypedCSV.explanation: Builds the same editable workbook and typed data.csv handoff as fromTypedRows, but reads the records from a captured CSV file with an exact declared header, column kinds and a reserved null token. The file bytes are copied into the run, so later verification does not depend on the original. Choose it when the table already exists as a file, such as a CSV written by another tool or a typed table handed over by an earlier Calc step; the quoting and null token follow the Apache Arrow adaptor's source dialect. Its file may be an earlier workflow step's CSV file or table artifact; the bytes are validated against the declared columns first. Workbook numbers keep 15 significant digits, so Data cells and the Summary MIN and MAX are checked to a relative 1e-14, while SUM, AVERAGE and STDEV allow relative 2e-8 plus 1e-12 of the column's largest magnitude; counts are exact and an all-zero column accepts only zero statistics.
pitfalls: Declare every CSV column, in file order, with the exact header text; nothing is inferred from the data.
The token (default \N) means missing in bare or quoted cells and cannot also be present text.
Numbers must be plain ASCII decimals with no spaces, separators, currency or percent signs; the old numeric readCSV still rejects the token and blanks.
A byte-order mark, line breaks inside cells, blank lines and empty text cells are rejected with the record and column.

fields.explanation: Create one numeric table, calculate fixed Data/Summary sheets in native Calc and independently verify XLSX, reopened ODS and CSV. Optional named requirements control acceptance.

/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis Calc document. It must be "schemaxis.calc/1"; it is not the LibreOffice version, and any installed LibreOffice that reports itself correctly can run it.

/properties/nodes.explanation: Declare exactly one source table per workbook. Use separate workflow operations for separate workbooks.

/properties/nodes/items.explanation: The single source node chooses a literal table or numeric CSV and names it for planning and inspection.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Build the workbook from explicit named columns and rectangular numeric rows. This is useful for small reproducible model tables or ledger fixtures.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Name this table source with an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, at most 64 characters.
fromRows: the table is written directly in this document as columns and rows. Switch to readCSV to load the same kind of table from a CSV file instead.
The literal table: columns gives the labels and rows gives the numeric records, in the order they appear on the Data sheet. Both are required; there are no other settings.
Give 1 to 64 unique literal column labels in data order. Labels are at most 128 characters and can describe units; they do not cause unit conversion.
One unique literal text label, at most 128 characters, without control characters. Labels beginning with = remain text; unit interpretation is authored.
Provide 2 to 10,000 numeric records, each matching the column count. Row order is preserved in Data and the CSV round trip.
One ordered numeric row with exactly one value for each column label. No automatic padding or column conversion occurs.
One finite numeric measurement within ±1e100. Booleans, text, missing values and authored formulas are rejected.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1.explanation: Build the workbook from a numeric CSV file, including a verified numeric table handed over from another workflow step. Choose this instead of fromRows when the data already exists as a file. The file bytes and their SHA-256 fingerprint are captured, so a reused run is only accepted while the file is unchanged.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Name this table source with an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, at most 64 characters.
readCSV: the table is read from a numeric CSV file named in options.file. Switch to fromRows to type a small table directly into the document.
The CSV source. Only file is needed: the header line becomes the column labels and each later line becomes one Data row.

Absolute path of a UTF-8, comma-separated file whose first line holds 1 to 64 distinct column labels and whose remaining 2 to 10,000 lines hold one finite number per column. The file must be a regular file of at most 8 MiB; it is copied into the run directory and read as plain text, never opened as a workbook.
pitfalls: Relative paths fail planning; give the full path, for example /data/run1/measurements.csv.
Semicolon-separated or locale-formatted numbers (such as 1,5) are not parsed; export with commas between fields and dots as decimal separators.
Empty cells, NaN, inf or any text below the header fail with INVALID_TABLE.

/properties/requirements.explanation: Optional list of up to 64 named numeric checks on cells of the calculated workbook. Each check is applied to the values Calc actually wrote in both analysis.xlsx and the reopened analysis.ods, and every check must pass in both for the run to succeed. Omit it to accept any correctly calculated workbook.
/properties/requirements.defaultMeaning: Omitted: no acceptance checks beyond the built-in verification of data and summary values.

/properties/requirements/items.explanation: One uniquely named fixed-cell numeric requirement. Native cell verification precedes acceptance; unmet checks retain diagnostic workbooks and block publication.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/0.explanation: An inclusive numeric cell bound. Supply minimum, maximum or both and inspect the signed distance to the closest bound in each native format.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/0/p.explanation: Name this requirement uniquely so failed assessments can identify the intended contract. Use an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, at most 64 characters.
cellBounds: check that one Data or Summary cell lies between an inclusive minimum and/or maximum. Use reconcile instead when several cells must add up (with coefficients) to a target.
Select one Data or Summary cell for the bound. Header labels are text and cannot satisfy a numeric requirement.

Select Data for original records or Summary for fixed count/sum/mean/min/max/sample-standard-deviation results. Data numeric rows start at 2; Summary rows follow the authored column order starting at 2.
Select a canonical uppercase A1 address without ranges or $ markers. Data spans up to BL10001; Summary up to G65. Missing cells and text labels fail separately from numeric limits.
Declare an inclusive minimum for the selected native value, finite within ±1e100 and expressed in that cell’s units. At least one bound is required; minimum cannot exceed maximum.
Declare an inclusive maximum for the selected native value, finite within ±1e100 and expressed in that cell’s units. At least one bound is required; minimum cannot exceed maximum.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/1.explanation: An explicit weighted reconciliation over distinct native numeric cells. Inspect value, target, absolute tolerance and signed margin separately for both formats.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/1/p.explanation: Name this requirement uniquely so failed assessments can identify the intended contract. Use an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, at most 64 characters.
reconcile: check that a weighted sum of 2 to 16 cells equals a target within an absolute tolerance, for example income minus costs equals zero. Use cellBounds instead to limit a single cell.
Select 2 to 16 distinct numeric cells and explicit nonzero coefficients. The author must ensure compatible units; the host sums the observed native values independently.
One explicit numeric cell and coefficient in the weighted reconciliation. Each cell appears at most once; header text is never converted to a number.

Select Data for original records or Summary for fixed count/sum/mean/min/max/sample-standard-deviation results. Data numeric rows start at 2; Summary rows follow the authored column order starting at 2.
Select a canonical uppercase A1 address without ranges or $ markers. Data spans up to BL10001; Summary up to G65. Missing cells and text labels fail separately from numeric limits.
Multiply this selected native value by a finite nonzero coefficient within ±1e6. Declare signs and any unit conversion explicitly; duplicate cell terms are rejected.
Declare the weighted-sum target in the reconciled units, finite within ±1e100. The default is zero, suitable for a declared balance residual.

Declare the maximum absolute weighted-sum difference from target, between zero and 1e100 in the reconciled units. Zero requires exact equality; choose a tolerance meaningful for native floating-point values.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/0/a.explanation: Lower-bound form: minimum is given, so the cell must be at least that value. A maximum may also be given to form a closed range.
Upper-bound form: maximum is given, so the cell must not exceed that value. A minimum may also be given to form a closed range.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2.explanation: Build the workbook from a labelled table written in this document, with a declared text or number kind for every column and explicit nulls for missing values.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Name this table source with an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, at most 64 characters.
fromTypedRows: the labelled table is written directly in this document. Switch to readTypedCSV to load the same kind of table from a CSV file, or to fromRows when every cell is numeric.

The literal labelled table: columns declares each name, kind and nullability; rows holds the records in column order; nullToken is the reserved missing-value marker used in the data.csv handoff. columns and rows are required.

Declare 1 to 64 columns in data order. Each has a unique name, a kind of text or number, and nullable (default false). Nothing is inferred from the values, and units belong in the name, for example Mass (g).
One column declaration: name, kind and optional nullable. Unknown keys such as unit or format are rejected rather than ignored.
Unique label of 1 to 128 characters, without control characters or text that workbook XML cannot represent. A leading =, +, - or @ is allowed and stays literal text. It cannot equal the null token.
pitfalls: Putting a unit in the name does not convert anything.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: text keeps exact characters and never enters arithmetic; number is a finite value within ±1e100 that receives COUNT, SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, sample STDEV and MISSING in the Summary sheet. There is no date, boolean, currency or automatic kind.
pitfalls: Choose text for identifiers, even when they look numeric; integers above 2^53 are rejected as numbers.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: false (the default) rejects a missing cell in this column; true allows null (or the null token in CSV), which becomes a blank workbook cell. A number column still needs at least two present values.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Omitted means false: a missing value is an error.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: The reserved marker for a missing cell in the typed data.csv and in readTypedCSV input; the default is \N, as in the Arrow adaptor. It is 1 to 16 visible characters, not a decimal number, with no comma, quote or space. Text equal to the token is rejected, so choose a token your text never uses.
pitfalls: A literal \N cannot be present text; pick another token if you need it.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Provide 1 to 10,000 records, each with one cell per declared column, at most 100,000 cells in total. Record order is preserved in Data and in data.csv; every record needs at least one present cell.
One ordered record with exactly one cell for each declared column, using null for a missing value. No padding, reordering or column conversion occurs.

One cell: a JSON string for a text column, a finite number for a number column, or null for a missing value in a nullable column. Booleans, objects, numeric strings, empty text and formulas are rejected, never converted.
pitfalls: Write IDs as strings, for example "00123"; 123 is not accepted in a text column.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: null: a missing value, stored as a blank cell. Allowed only in a column declared nullable.
A finite number within ±1e100 for a number column. A zero is a real measurement, not a missing value.
Text of 1 to 1,024 characters for a text column, exactly as written (no trimming or Unicode normalization). Control characters and empty text are rejected; =1+2 stays literal text.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3.explanation: Build the workbook from a typed CSV file: exact declared header, declared text or number columns and a reserved null token. The file bytes and SHA-256 fingerprint are captured, so a reused run is only accepted while the file is unchanged.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Name this table source with an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, at most 64 characters.
readTypedCSV: the labelled table is read from the CSV file named in options.file. Switch to fromTypedRows to type a small table into the document.
The typed CSV source: file is the CSV path, columns declares each header name, kind and nullability in file order, and nullToken is the reserved missing-value marker. file and columns are required.

Absolute path of a regular UTF-8 CSV of at most 8 MiB: no byte-order mark, comma-delimited, LF or CRLF records, cells bare or wholly double-quoted with "" for a quote, first record equal to the declared names. The file is copied into the run directory and never opened as a workbook; a relative path fails planning. In a workflow it can be bound to an earlier step's CSV file or table artifact, for example {"$artifact": "summary", "index": 2}; a file kind does not make the bytes trusted, so the declared header, kinds and null token are checked before any native work.
pitfalls: Line breaks inside cells, blank lines, trailing commas and ragged records are rejected with the record number.
A changed file, header, kind or token is a different input and cannot reuse an earlier run.
Binding a non-CSV artifact (such as a SQLite database) or one with an empty label, padded number or renamed header stops with INVALID_TABLE; declare the producer's own header names and null marker.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Declare 1 to 64 columns in data order. Each has a unique name, a kind of text or number, and nullable (default false). Nothing is inferred from the values, and units belong in the name, for example Mass (g). The names must equal the CSV header exactly, in file order.
One column declaration: name, kind and optional nullable. Unknown keys such as unit or format are rejected rather than ignored.
Unique label of 1 to 128 characters, without control characters or text that workbook XML cannot represent. A leading =, +, - or @ is allowed and stays literal text. It cannot equal the null token.
pitfalls: Putting a unit in the name does not convert anything.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: text keeps exact characters and never enters arithmetic; number is a finite value within ±1e100 that receives COUNT, SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, sample STDEV and MISSING in the Summary sheet. There is no date, boolean, currency or automatic kind.
pitfalls: Choose text for identifiers, even when they look numeric; integers above 2^53 are rejected as numbers.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: false (the default) rejects a missing cell in this column; true allows null (or the null token in CSV), which becomes a blank workbook cell. A number column still needs at least two present values.
/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.defaultMeaning: Omitted means false: a missing value is an error.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: The reserved marker for a missing cell in the typed data.csv and in readTypedCSV input; the default is \N, as in the Arrow adaptor. It is 1 to 16 visible characters, not a decimal number, with no comma, quote or space. Text equal to the token is rejected, so choose a token your text never uses.
pitfalls: A literal \N cannot be present text; pick another token if you need it.
